---
title: "check-avoided-words.yml"
---

Diff-scoped check that flags words and phrases a style source
advises against, in `.qmd` and `.md` prose.
This is [psw#418](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/psw/pull/418).

## Rules

- **Position words.**
  `above` or `below` used for a place in the document ("the table above",
  "as shown below"); refer to the result by its label.
  Source: Google developer documentation style guide, word list, entries
  "above" and "below".
  "A value above the threshold" is a comparison and passes.
- **Effort words.**
  `just`, `easy`, `easily`.
  Source: the same word list.
  `just before`, `just after`, `just as`, `just like`, `just then`,
  `just enough`, `just in time`, `just once` and `just now` pass.
- **Time-relative words.**
  `currently`, `recently`, `nowadays`, `at present`, `at the moment`,
  `these days`.
  Source: Google, "Timeless documentation".
  The guide lists `now` and `new` too, but this check does not flag them,
  because "now we compute" and the term "new observation" are correct uses a
  regex cannot tell apart.
  `recently` is psw's own extension.
- **Generic placeholders.**
  A domain, codomain, range or sample space named by
  a bare capital letter ("domain A") or by "some" ("some domain").
  Name the specific set, such as "the range of X".
  Source: psw's "be as specific as feasible" (psw#427).
  A regex cannot know whether a specific object exists,
  so a finding only asks the author to check.
- **Back-references to a setup.**
  "The setup of @exr-x" or "the same setup as".
  Name the data, variables or model the part reuses.
  Source: psw's "Talk about the ideas, not the notes" (psw#442).
- **"Score" for a linear predictor.**
  "score" or "scores" on a line that also has `\eta`, "linear predictor",
  "log-odds", "logit", "sigmoid", or "logistic function".
  Write "log-odds" for a logistic regression and "linear predictor" for a GLM in general.
  The statistical score keeps its name, so "score function", "score equation",
  "score test", "Brier score", "z-score", "F1 score", "component score",
  a link whose text is "score", and a line holding `#def-score` pass.
  Source: Ezra's rule (gha#1568).
- **Trailing parenthetical links.**
  A crossref after a word, such as `differentiable at $c$ (@def-differentiable)`,
  or a `([why](url))` link after a claim.
  Link the term itself, or make the whole claim the link text.
  `(see @thm-x)` passes, since no word can carry that link.
  Source: Ezra's review of mds, 2026-11-02 (gha#1402).
  This rule fails the run whatever `fail` says.
- **The word "thing".**
  `thing` or `things` as a whole word; `something`, `anything`, and `nothing` pass.
  Name the object, quantity, step, or idea instead.
  Source: psw's "Say which thing" (gha#1454).
  This rule also fails the run whatever `fail` says,
  and `<!-- check-avoided-words: allow -->` exempts a deliberate use.
  A consumer on the `v3` tag sees its check turn red
  on any added line containing the word.

The other rules fail by default; set `fail` to false to make them warn.

The check does not flag a code fence or code span, an HTML comment, YAML
front matter, or a line carrying, or following,
`<!-- check-avoided-words: allow -->`.
It reports at most one finding per rule per line.

## Scope

Only lines a pull request adds are reported,
so existing uses are not reflagged on every unrelated edit.
An added line whose exact text was also deleted in the same diff
counts as moved rather than new.

With no `base-ref`, or when the diff cannot be computed
(a shallow clone, an unresolvable ref),
the check skips with a warning.
It never falls back to a whole-tree scan.
Set `whole-tree: true` to scan every tracked file in full on purpose.

Every run prints how many lines and files it examined.

## Inputs

| Input            | Type    | Default | Description |
| ---------------- | ------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `globs`          | string  | `'*.qmd *.md'` | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to check (recursive by default). |
| `paths-ignore`   | string  | `''`    | Comma- or newline-separated glob patterns (relative paths) to skip. Supports `*`, `?` and recursive `**`. |
| `fail`           | boolean | `true`  | Fail the workflow when an avoided word is found. Set `false` for warnings only; a trailing parenthetical link and the words "thing" and "things" always fail. |
| `whole-tree`     | boolean | `false` | Scan every tracked file in full instead of only a PR's added lines. |
| `python-version` | string  | `'3.x'` | Python version to set up. |
| `runs-on` | string | empty (`CI_RUNNER` variable, else `ubuntu-latest`) | Runner label for the job. Use a self-hosted label only for a private repository; never for a public one, whose pull requests can run arbitrary code on it ([#1167](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1167)). |

## Permissions

Only `contents: read` (the default), so no `permissions:` block is needed.

## Example

```yaml
# Copy to .github/workflows/check-avoided-words.yml in your repo.
name: Check avoided words

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  check:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/check-avoided-words.yml@v3
    # with:
    #   globs: '*.qmd *.md'                     # pathspecs to check (recursive)
    #   paths-ignore: 'chapters/outtakes/**'    # skip known-noisy paths
    #   fail: false                             # warn on all but the always-failing rules (defaults to true)
    #   whole-tree: true                        # scan every line, not just a PR's additions
    #   runs-on: private-runner                # self-hosted runner label (private repositories only)
```

See
[`examples/check-avoided-words.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/check-avoided-words.yml)
for the full caller stub.
